newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Dollar hits 2-1/2 year high on Japan woes.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Dollar hits 2-1/2 year high on Japan woes.

text.p: The dollar hit 2-1/2 year highs against the Japanese yen on Monday, boosted by renewed signs of a faltering economic recovery in Japan.
The dollar peaked at 111.66 yen after investors began to liquidate long yen positions on perceptions of slowing Japanese growth and a widening U.S.-Japan interest rate gap.
The weekend meeting of Group of Seven (G7) nations in Washington also underpinned the U.S. currency with finance ministers and central bank chiefs expressing satisfaction with current exchange rates.

"The key factor is that against a background of a modest recovery in Japan, yields will remain low encouraging Japanese investors to move funds overseas," said Gerard Lyons, chief economist at DKB International in London.
By 1400 GMT the dollar was quoted at 111.45 yen and 1.5256, compared with Friday's late European levels of 110.78 yen and 1.5239 marks.
European share markets began the week in a subdued mood, but London and Paris both reversed early weakness before Wall Street opened firm. Frankfurt remained weak, however.

Gold came back under pressure in Europe and later in New York as the bearish sentiment seen on Friday deepened. It fixed in London at $379.00 in the afternoon after $379.30 in the morning, the first fixes below the psychological $380 level since September 6 last year and compared with $380.70 on Friday afternoon.
"There's a general concern in Europe that it's not over yet," one trader said.
Japan's economic prospects provided the major impetus for the dollar after August preliminary industrial output figures showed a larger-than-expected decline of 1.9 percent.

"Japan's economy has been seen as coming out of recession slowly and steadily but the industrial output figures were lower than expected," said Teddy Dewitt, bond strategist at Societe Generale Strauss Turnbull in London.
Comments by Japan's Finance Minister Wataru Kubo and Bank of Japan governor Yasuo Matsushita were seen encouraging Japanese institutional investors to seek higher returns overseas.
"There is a lot of talk of a substantial amount of capital flowing out of Japan in the second half of the fiscal year which starts Tuesday," said a currency dealer at a German bank in London.
The London stock market reversed modest early losses by mid-afternoon in a session characterised by stockpicking and low volumes.
The FTSE 100 share index, which dropped as low as 3,934.4 points, swung back to positive territory by early afternoon to stand nearly eight points up at 3,954 by 1400 GMT.
"This is a loose end day. Investors are saying, it's the end of the quarter, we don't want commitments just now," said Roger Monson, strategist at Daiwa Europe Ltd.
Traders agreed, saying investors had chosen to sit back to await key data from the United States, including the NAPM index on Tuesday and Friday's important payrolls data.
French shares opened slightly weaker on profit-taking ahead of the expiry of September futures contracts later in the day, but by mid-afternoon the CAC-40 index was well up.
It climbed strongly as Wall Street opened firm and was 23 points, or just over one percent ahead, at 1400 GMT.
German shares ended bourse trade lower amid evidence of profit-taking. The 30-share blue chip DAX index ended down 7.19 points, or 0.27 percent, at 2,651.85 points.

Dealers blamed the fall on a mild bout of profit-taking after the DAX surged to record highs last week but said many investors steered clear of the market in the absence of any significant corporate news.
CURRENCIES AT 1400 GMT
The was trading at 111.45 yen and 1.5256 marks, compared with Friday's late European levels of 110.78 yen and 1.5239 marks.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1400 GMT
LONDON - The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was up 7.6 points at 3,954.0.
PARIS - The CAC-40 share index was up 23.09 at 2,130.14.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index closed down 7.19 points at 2,651.85. In later computerised trade, the IBI DAX was down 6.07 at 2,653.79 PRECIOUS METALS AT 1400
Gold fixed at $379.00, its first move below $380 since Sept 6, last year and compared with $380.70 on Friday afternoon. Silver was five cents easier at $4.88.
